terms.grammar: the genitive plural of oculus, beside the noun it describes, often set against aurium
evidence: Sen. Ep. 88.22: ad voluptātem oculōrum atque aurium (M-O s.v. art)
terms.comment: Classical Latin has no adjective for “visual”: it says “of the eyes”, as it says animī for mental (see mental). The visual arts are Seneca’s arts that aim ad voluptātem oculōrum (Morgan–Owens).

terms.grammar: the genitive of vīsus, the sense of sight
terms.comment: Where the sense itself is meant: vīsūs aciēs, keenness of sight (see vision).
Late Latin (Cassiodorus); Morgan–Owens gives it for the visual arts beside Seneca’s periphrasis.

phrases.latin: erat in tantā cālīgine major ūsus aurium quam oculōrum
phrases.english: in such thick fog the ears were of more use than the eyes

phrases.latin: plūra … sunt … in sēnsibus oculōrum quam in verbīs vōcibusque colōrum discrīmina
phrases.english: the eyes tell more colours apart than words and names can
